title: Normalized scalar comparison for actual coefficient sections
statement: Let $l$ be prime, $E$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_l$, $W$ a scheme, and $n\in\mathbf N$. Use the completed and finite coefficient sheaves and their exact scalar restriction from [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and the section functors and comparison equations from [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. There is a natural isomorphism from finite derived scalar restriction followed by integral derived sections to finite derived sections. On every finite-coefficient cochain complex $I$, its composite with the completed-sections comparison unit and the scalar-restriction localization comparison equals the derived image of the ordinary scalar-sections transformation followed by the finite-sections comparison unit. The ordinary transformation is the unique comparison taking a map from the completed module unit to the finite module-unit map whose value at one is the same section.

source.place: Tags 079P, 0941 and 0D6E; the normalized coefficient sections construction.

proof.text: A map from the module unit is determined by its value at one. Identify these maps with compatible sections and then with the limit of the underlying presheaf. Restriction leaves this underlying presheaf unchanged, so these identifications define the ordinary scalar comparison and its value-at-one formula.

Transport the proved restriction-of-scalars sections acyclicity theorem along that identification. For a K-injective finite complex, resolve its restricted complex by a K-injective complex. Sections of the resolution map are a quasi-isomorphism; naturality and invertibility of the comparison unit on the resolving complex show invertibility on the restricted complex.

Record the actual section functors and site units as right-derived pairs. The exact scalar-restriction composite is a right derivation by the preceding invertibility. The ordinary scalar isomorphism induces a universal right-derived isomorphism, whose unit identity is exactly the displayed comparison equation on every complex.
